family.name: HR Business Partner
family.summary: Attrition is up and the business head wants a 10% raise for everyone: find the one team and manager behind it, choose a fix, and catch the confidentiality breach in a new policy.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: What is really driving attrition?
stages.summary: Find that attrition is concentrated in one team under a new manager, with workload spiralling, not a company-wide pay problem. Think aloud.

stages.title: What do you recommend?
stages.summary: Recommend a fix to the business head. Tests judgement, fairness and cost. Think aloud.

stages.title: Six weeks later
stages.summary: Consequences of their recommendation. Tests adapting and handling people.

stages.title: Review a new policy draft
stages.summary: A policy that shares named exit interview comments with managers and punishes all exits. Think aloud.

stages.title: Talking points for the manager (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Prepare a hard conversation with the manager using AI. Catches vague or accusatory scripts.

stages.title: A people problem you solved
stages.summary: A real people issue they handled. Checks specificity and ownership.

brief.text: You're the HR business partner for the delivery side of **Carelink**, a healthcare services company. The business head says: "Attrition is killing us. Let's give everyone a 10% raise." That would cost ₹6,00,00,000 a year.

items: In Patient Support, a new manager was promoted from within 14 months ago. 67% of that team's leavers were rated high performers.
Exit interviews in Patient Support: 67% mention "my manager", 50% workload, 26% pay.
Patient Support now handles about 45 cases per person a week, up from 23, because leavers weren't replaced.
Market data: your pay is 4% below the median for these roles, the same for every team.
The latest engagement survey shows Patient Support down 18 points; other teams are flat.

brief.text: The company and numbers are fictional, and every candidate gets a slightly different version. A calculator is fine.

prompt.text: Tell us about a manager who brought out the best in you.
Keep it under 45 seconds. This one is not scored; it just gets you talking.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: **What is really driving attrition here, and is the business head's fix the right one?** Use the data.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

choices.label: Give everyone a 10% raise, as the business head wants
Targeted retention for key people plus support and coaching for the manager
Run stay interviews in the team before deciding anything
Move the manager out of the role now

prompt.text: **What do you recommend?** Pick one, say roughly what it costs, and how you would handle the manager fairly.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Give everyone a 10% raise, as the business head wants"

prompt.text: The raise went out. Three more people left Patient Support this month, two of them high performers, and their exit interviews again mention the manager. Finance asks what the ₹6,00,00,000 achieved.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Targeted retention for key people plus support and coaching for the manager"

prompt.text: The manager feels singled out and tells the business head that HR is "building a case" against them. Meanwhile one retained high performer says she was promised a promotion that hasn't happened.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Run stay interviews in the team before deciding anything"

prompt.text: The stay interviews confirm workload and the manager. But two more people resigned during the four weeks they took, and the business head asks why HR "only talked".
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Move the manager out of the role now"

prompt.text: The manager was moved. They have raised a formal grievance saying no feedback was ever given. The team now has no manager, and the business head wants HR to "find someone fast".
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: The business head drafted a policy to "make managers own attrition". **Name the problems, worst first, and the harm each could cause.** Then say what you would change.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

material.text: Draft policy: manager accountability for attrition

items: Every manager receives the full exit interview of each leaver, with the leaver's name, every month.
Managers with any leaver in a quarter lose 20% of their bonus.
Managers must hold a monthly one-to-one with each team member.
HR publishes a ranking of managers by attrition on the intranet.

stages.title: Talking points for the manager (AI allowed)

prompt.text: Use any AI tool you like for this one. We are assessing how you use it, not whether you do.
Write your talking points (under 200 words) for a conversation with the Patient Support manager: what you've seen, how you'll support them, what you expect, and by when.

items: Paste your final answer.
Paste your full AI conversation, or write "none".
In 2–3 lines, say what you kept, changed or rejected from the AI and why.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: **Tell us about a people problem in a team that you helped solve.** What did you see, what did you do, and what would you do differently?
Specifics such as numbers and timelines matter more than polish.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.
